judgments.yea_description: Voted to accept the final version of House Bill 1247. The Georgia Bureaucratic Deference Elimination Act bars courts and hearing officers from deferring to a state agency's reading of the law. Under the Red Tape Rollback Act of 2026, lawmakers can void an agency rule by majority vote instead of two-thirds, and most agencies must analyze their rules for the state budget office every five years from 2028. It also opens to the public any settlement of a workplace claim, such as sexual harassment, against a legislator, and makes privately funded metro-Atlanta shelters near schools, parks, or playgrounds join the state homeless data system. The Georgia House agreed 98-70, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to accept the final version of House Bill 1247. The Georgia Bureaucratic Deference Elimination Act stops courts from favoring a state agency's own reading of laws and rules, changes rulemaking steps, and makes agencies review every rule for the state budget office under the Red Tape Rollback Act of 2026. It also opens to the public any settlement of an unlawful employment practice claim against a member of the General Assembly, naming the member but not the claimant. A separate part requires some privately funded groups that shelter or serve homeless people to join the state homeless information system. That duty reaches only groups within 1,000 feet of a school, college, child care center, public park, or playground in one metro area, and skips groups that served fewer than ten people last year. The Georgia Senate agreed 34-18, and it became law.
